records.gloss: For the director. A psalm of David.
pieces: For the music director. A psalm of David.

L.1: For the director. A psalm of David.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1, Readable says what a psalm is.

records.heading: Heavens and instruction tell God's glory

records.source: הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם מְֽסַפְּרִ֥ים כְּבֽוֹד־אֵ֑ל וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דָ֗יו מַגִּ֥יד הָרָקִֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: The heavens [are] recounting [the] glory of God, and [the] work of his hands the expanse [is] declaring.
pieces: The heavens tell over and over how glorious God is; the vault of the sky makes known what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands have made.

L.2: The heavens are recounting the glory of God, and the work of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands the expanse is declaring.

R.2: The sky keeps telling how great and glorious God is. Everything up there shows what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made.

decisions.choice: are recounting, is declaring: they never stop
decisions.reason: Both verbs are participles, for something that goes on and on. The sky is pictured as a speaker who tells God's glory without a break.

decisions.choice: the expanse: the dome of the sky
decisions.reason: The word (raqia') is the expanse God made to separate the waters above from the waters below (Genesis 1:6-8), the sky seen as a great vault over the earth.

decisions.choice: God, the work of his hands: the Creator of Genesis 1
decisions.reason: The first half of the psalm praises God (here 'El) as Creator; from verse 8 it praises the LORD for his instruction. The two halves together say that God makes himself known in the world he made and in the word he gave.

decisions.choice: the vault of the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced names the picture (m2) in words a listener can see; "firmament" is no longer in common use.

records.source: י֣וֹם לְ֭יוֹם יַבִּ֣יעַֽ אֹ֑מֶר וְלַ֥יְלָה לְּ֝לַ֗יְלָה יְחַוֶּה־דָּֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night declares knowledge.
pieces: Each day passes the message on to the next; each night hands its knowledge to the night that follows.

L.3: Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night makes known knowledge.

R.3: Every day passes the news on to the next day. Every night shares what it knows with the next night.

decisions.choice: day to day: one day hands the message to the next
decisions.reason: The message is pictured as passed along a line, each day telling the next and each night the next, so that it never stops.

decisions.choice: pours forth: bubbles out like a spring
decisions.reason: The verb (naba') is used of a spring that bubbles up (Proverbs 18:4): the speech flows out freely.

records.source: אֵֽין־אֹ֭מֶר וְאֵ֣ין דְּבָרִ֑ים בְּ֝לִ֗י נִשְׁמָ֥ע קוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: There is no speech and there are no words; not heard [is] their voice.
pieces: There is no speech, there are no words; nothing of their voice reaches the ear.

L.4: There is no speech, and there are no words; their voice is not heard.

R.4: They do not speak or use words. You cannot hear their voice with your ears.

decisions.choice: no speech, no words: the sky's message is silent
alternatives: there is no speech or language where their voice is not heard
decisions.reason: The verse says that the heavens tell God's glory without words or sound; their message is seen, not heard. It can also be read as saying that there is no language in which their voice is not heard, but the Hebrew more simply means that they speak in silence.

records.source: בְּכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ׀יָ֘צָ֤א קַוָּ֗ם וּבִקְצֵ֣ה תֵ֭בֵל מִלֵּיהֶ֑ם לַ֝שֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ שָֽׂם־אֹ֥הֶל בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: In all the earth has gone out their line, and at [the] end of [the] world their words; for the sun he has set a tent in them.
pieces: Even so, their line runs out over the whole earth, their words to the far edge of the world. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set up a tent for the sun,

L.5: In all the earth their line has gone out, and to the end of the world their words. For the sun {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set a tent in them,

R.5: But their message reaches the whole earth. Their words go out to the ends of the world. God has set up a home for the sun in the sky.

decisions.choice: their line: a measuring line, marking out their reach
decisions.reason: The word (qav) is a measuring line: the heavens' message is stretched out over the whole earth. The ancient Greek translation has "their sound", which suits "their words" in the next line and may come from reading a slightly different word.

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 10:18
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this line, in the wording of the ancient Greek translation, to say that the message about Christ has gone out to the whole world (Romans 10:18).

decisions.choice: he has set: God; in them: in the heavens
decisions.reason: "He" is God of verse 2, and "in them" are the heavens, where God has pitched a tent for the sun to rest in at night.

decisions.choice: their message
decisions.reason: Readable says what the line stands for (m1).

decisions.choice: God; in the sky
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts and where (m3).

records.source: וְה֗וּא כְּ֭חָתָן יֹצֵ֣א מֵחֻפָּת֑וֹ יָשִׂ֥ישׂ כְּ֝גִבּ֗וֹר לָר֥וּץ אֹֽרַח׃
records.gloss: And it [is] like a bridegroom coming out from his chamber; it rejoices like a mighty [man] to run [the] path.
pieces: and the sun comes out like a bridegroom from the wedding room and runs its course with the joy of a strong warrior.

L.6: and it [is] like a bridegroom coming out from his chamber; it rejoices like a mighty [man] to run [its] course.

R.6: The sun rises like a happy bridegroom coming out of his room on his wedding day. It is like a strong runner who loves to race across the sky.

decisions.choice: his chamber: the wedding room
decisions.reason: The word (chuppah) is the room or canopy where a bridegroom and bride first meet as husband and wife (Joel 2:16). The sun comes out at dawn as fresh and glad as a bridegroom.

decisions.choice: a mighty man: a strong warrior or champion
decisions.reason: The word (gibbor) is a strong man, often a warrior. The sun runs its daily course across the sky with a champion's strength and joy.

decisions.choice: the sun
decisions.reason: "It" is the sun of verse 5; Balanced and Readable name it.

records.source: מִקְצֵ֤ה הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם׀מֽוֹצָא֗וֹ וּתְקוּפָת֥וֹ עַל־קְצוֹתָ֑ם וְאֵ֥ין נִ֝סְתָּ֗ר מֵֽחַמָּתוֹ׃
records.gloss: From [the] end of the heavens [is] its going out, and its circuit [is] to their ends, and there is nothing hidden from its heat.
pieces: It sets out from one edge of the heavens and circles round to the other; nothing escapes its heat.

L.7: From [one] end of the heavens [is] its going out, and its circuit [is] to their [other] end, and nothing is hidden from its heat.

R.7: It starts at one edge of the sky and goes all the way across. Nothing can hide from its heat.

decisions.choice: nothing is hidden from its heat
decisions.reason: As the sun's heat reaches everything, so the LORD's instruction, praised in the next verses, searches everything, even sins hidden from the one who does them (verse 13, which uses the same word "hidden").

records.source: תּ֘וֹרַ֤ת יְהוָ֣ה תְּ֭מִימָה מְשִׁ֣יבַת נָ֑פֶשׁ עֵד֥וּת יְהוָ֥ה נֶ֝אֱמָנָ֗ה מַחְכִּ֥ימַת פֶּֽתִי׃
records.gloss: [The] instruction of YHWH [is] perfect, bringing back [the] soul; [the] testimony of YHWH [is] reliable, making wise [the] simple.
pieces: The instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is whole and without fault; it brings back life. What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has declared can be trusted; it makes the naive wise.

L.8: The instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] perfect, bringing back [the] soul; the testimony of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] reliable, making wise the simple.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s teaching is perfect. It gives people new life. What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tells us is true and can be trusted. It gives wisdom to people who have not yet learned.

decisions.choice: instruction, testimony: names for God's word
decisions.reason: Verses 8-10 give six names for what the LORD has spoken: instruction (torah), testimony ('edut, his solemn declaration of what he requires), precepts, commandment, fear, and judgments. Torah is teaching and guidance, more than law in a narrow sense.

decisions.choice: bringing back the soul: restoring life and strength
decisions.reason: To bring back the soul (nefesh) is to give new life to someone who is faint, as food does (Lamentations 1:11).

decisions.choice: perfect; the simple
decisions.reason: Perfect (tamim) means whole, with nothing missing or flawed. The simple (peti) are the inexperienced, easily led astray, whom wisdom seeks to teach (Proverbs 1:4).

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: As in 1:2, Readable says "teaching" for torah (m1).

records.source: פִּקּ֘וּדֵ֤י יְהוָ֣ה יְ֭שָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי־לֵ֑ב מִצְוַ֥ת יְהוָ֥ה בָּ֝רָ֗ה מְאִירַ֥ת עֵינָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: [The] precepts of YHWH [are] upright, making glad [the] heart; [the] commandment of YHWH [is] pure, making bright [the] eyes.
pieces: The charges {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lays down are right and fill the heart with joy; the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is clear and makes the eyes shine.

L.9: The precepts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] upright, making the heart glad; the commandment of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] pure, giving light to the eyes.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s rules are right, and they make people glad. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s commands are clear. They bring new strength, like light coming back into tired eyes.

decisions.choice: precepts, commandment: what God charges people to do
decisions.reason: Precepts (piqqudim) are the charges an overseer lays down; commandment (mitsvah) is an order. Both are words for God's instruction (verse 8).

decisions.choice: making the eyes bright: giving new life
decisions.reason: Bright eyes are a sign of fresh strength: when tired Jonathan ate honey, "his eyes brightened" (1 Samuel 14:27). God's command revives like that.

decisions.choice: they bring new strength, like light coming back into tired eyes
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

records.source: יִרְאַ֤ת יְהוָ֨ה׀טְהוֹרָה֮ עוֹמֶ֪דֶת לָ֫עַ֥ד מִֽשְׁפְּטֵי־יְהוָ֥ה אֱמֶ֑ת צָֽדְק֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃
records.gloss: [The] fear of YHWH [is] clean, standing forever; [the] judgments of YHWH [are] truth; they are righteous altogether.
pieces: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is clean and lasts for all time; the rulings of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are true, and every one of them is just.

L.10: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] clean, standing forever; the judgments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] truth; they are righteous altogether.

R.10: Respecting {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe is pure and good, and it lasts forever. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s decisions are true. Every one of them is fair.

decisions.choice: the fear of the LORD: reverence that obeys
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is the awe and reverence that shape a whole life (Proverbs 1:7). Here, in a list of names for God's word, it stands for the way of life that his instruction teaches.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings
decisions.reason: The word (mishpatim) means the decisions of a judge, and so the rulings God has given his people.

decisions.choice: respecting the LORD with awe
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fear of the LORD means (m1), since "fear" alone can sound like terror.

records.source: הַֽנֶּחֱמָדִ֗ים מִ֭זָּהָב וּמִפַּ֣ז רָ֑ב וּמְתוּקִ֥ים מִ֝דְּבַ֗שׁ וְנֹ֣פֶת צוּפִֽים׃
records.gloss: The [ones] desirable more than gold and more than much fine gold, and sweeter than honey and [the] drippings of [the] honeycombs.
pieces: They are worth wanting more than gold, more than a great hoard of fine gold; sweeter than honey, sweeter than honey fresh from the comb.

L.11: [They are] more desirable than gold, and than much fine gold, and sweeter than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb.

R.11: They are worth more than gold, even the purest gold. They taste sweeter than honey, even honey straight from the honeycomb.

decisions.choice: they: the LORD's words of verses 8-10
decisions.reason: The verse continues the praise of the LORD's instruction, judgments and commands.

decisions.choice: fine gold: refined, pure gold
decisions.reason: The word (paz) is gold of the highest quality (21:4).

records.source: גַּֽם־עַ֭בְדְּךָ נִזְהָ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְרָ֗ם עֵ֣קֶב רָֽב׃
records.gloss: Also your servant [is] warned by them; in keeping them [is] great reward.
pieces: They also warn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and those who keep them gain a great reward.

L.12: Moreover {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is warned by them; in keeping them [there is] great reward.

R.12: They warn me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. And there is great reward in obeying them.

decisions.choice: warned: taught and cautioned
decisions.reason: The verb (zahar) means to warn or instruct; the same root can mean to shine (Daniel 12:3), which suits "giving light to the eyes" in verse 9.

decisions.choice: reward: what follows as a result
decisions.reason: The word ('eqev) is what comes at the end, the outcome of a life; here a good one.

decisions.choice: your servant: the psalmist speaks to God
decisions.reason: From here to the end the psalmist turns to speak to the LORD and calls himself his servant.

records.gloss: Errors, who will discern? From hidden [ones] acquit me.
pieces: Who can catch all their own mistakes? Hold me clear of faults hidden even from me.

L.13: Errors, who can discern [them]? From hidden [faults] declare me innocent.

R.13: No one can see all the wrong things they do. Free me from blame for the sins I do not even know about.

decisions.choice: errors: wrongs done without meaning to
decisions.reason: The word (shegi'ot) comes from a root meaning to stray or go wrong by mistake; the law makes a place for such sins (Leviticus 4:2).

decisions.choice: hidden: faults hidden from the one who commits them
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 7: nothing is hidden from the sun's heat, and the psalmist asks to be cleared even of what is hidden from himself.

decisions.choice: acquit me: declare me free of guilt
decisions.reason: The verb (naqah) means to hold someone innocent or free from punishment.

records.source: גַּ֤ם מִזֵּדִ֨ים׀חֲשֹׂ֬ךְ עַבְדֶּ֗ךָ אַֽל־יִמְשְׁלוּ־בִ֣י אָ֣ז אֵיתָ֑ם וְ֝נִקֵּ֗יתִי מִפֶּ֥שַֽׁע רָֽב׃
records.gloss: Also from presumptuous [ones] keep back your servant; let them not rule over me; then I will be blameless, and I will be innocent of great transgression.
pieces: Hold {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant back from arrogant sins too; let them never be my master. Then I will be whole and clear of any great rebellion.

L.14: Also from presumptuous [sins] hold back {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; let them not rule over me. Then I will be blameless, and I will be innocent of great transgression.

R.14: Keep me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, from sinning on purpose out of pride. Do not let those sins control me. Then I will be without blame and free from great rebellion.

decisions.choice: presumptuous ones: proud, willful sins
decisions.reason: The word (zedim) means the arrogant. It may mean arrogant people who would lead the psalmist astray, but beside the "errors" of verse 13 it more likely means sins done in pride and on purpose (Numbers 15:30).

decisions.choice: transgression: rebellion
decisions.reason: The word (pesha') means a breaking away, rebellion against God.

decisions.choice: arrogant sins (B); sinning on purpose out of pride (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the sense chosen in m1.

records.source: יִֽהְי֥וּ לְרָצ֨וֹן׀אִמְרֵי־פִ֡י וְהֶגְי֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ יְ֝הוָ֗ה צוּרִ֥י וְגֹאֲלִֽי׃
records.gloss: Let them be for acceptance, [the] words of my mouth and [the] meditation of my heart, before you, YHWH, my rock and my redeemer.
pieces: May what my mouth speaks and what my heart ponders be welcome before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock and my redeemer.

L.15: Let them be acceptable, the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart, before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock and my redeemer.

R.15: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my rock, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who rescues me. I pray that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be pleased with my words and with the thoughts of my heart.

decisions.choice: for acceptance: welcome, like an offering
decisions.reason: The phrase (lerason) is used of sacrifices that God accepts (Leviticus 1:3). The psalmist offers his words and thoughts as a gift.

decisions.choice: my rock and my redeemer
decisions.reason: A rock is a place of safety (18:3). The redeemer (go'el) is the near relative who buys back a family member or his land (Leviticus 25:25): God is the one who sets his people free.

decisions.choice: meditation: what the heart turns over quietly
decisions.reason: The word (higgayon) is from the verb of 1:2, for murmuring or pondering.

decisions.choice: the one who rescues me
decisions.reason: Readable says what a redeemer does (m2).
